A consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Howard Bison men's basketball|Howard University]], becoming the highest-ranked player in the modern recruiting era to commit to a [[Historically black colleges and universities|historically black college or university]] (HBCU). Born in [[Nairobi]], Maker grew up in [[Perth]], Western Australia, before playing high school basketball in North America. He is the cousin of basketball players [[Thon Maker|Thon]] and [[Matur Maker]]. ==Early life== Maker was born in [[Nairobi]], Kenya, to [[South Sudan]]ese parents and immigrated to [[Perth]], Western Australia, when he was one year old.{{cite web |last1=Kwan |first1=Biwa |title=How this Australian basketball prodigy hopes to inspire minorities by turning down America's biggest universities |url=https://www.sbs.com.au/news/how-this-australian-basketball-prodigy-hopes-to-inspire-minorities-by-turning-down-america-s-biggest-universities |website=SBS |access-date=30 November 2020 |date=4 July 2020}} Before focusing on basketball, he mainly took interest in [[association football|football]] as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]] and often played [[beach soccer]] with his friends. Maker played for Quinns Football club alongside his older brothers. Maker attended St. Andrews Catholic Primary School and joined Irene McCormack Catholic College for high school. He was drawn to basketball in part because of his exceptional height.{{cite web |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=Makur may end up as the next Maker in the NBA, but he's in a league of his own |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/makur-may-end-up-as-the-next-maker-in-the-nba-but-hes-in-a-league-of-his-own/news-story/9c2446a337fd08dcec8eab066f8c8532 |work=[[Fox Sports (Australia)|Fox Sports]] |accessdate=30 July 2019 |date=8 February 2019}} ==High school career== In 2015, Maker moved to the United States and enrolled for his freshman year at [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (California)|Chaminade College Preparatory School]] in [[West Hills, Los Angeles]].{{cite web |last1=Sondheimer |first1=Eric |title=Boys' basketball: 6–11 freshman Makur Maker enrolls at Chaminade |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vi-boys-basketball-6-11-freshman-makur-maker-enrolls-at-chaminade-20150825-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |accessdate=31 July 2019 |date=25 August 2015}} As a result, he was forced to live away from his family for many years. As a freshman, Maker averaged 9.5 points, 8.2 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Thon Maker's Cousin is 6'11 and has Made it to Canada, joining The Tech Academy Titans |url=https://northpolehoops.com/2016/09/28/thon-makers-cousin-is-611-and-has-made-it-to-canada-joining-the-tech-academy-titans/ |publisher=North Pole Hoops |accessdate=31 July 2019 |date=28 September 2016}} In 2016, he transferred to The Tech Academy, a [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] in [[Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario]].{{cite web |title=Thon Maker's 6–11 cousin joins Prolific Prep North in Canada |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/thon-makers-6-11-cousin-joins-prolific-prep-north-in-canada |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=31 July 2019 |date=29 September 2016}} He was drawn to the program by his cousins, basketball players [[Thon Maker|Thon]] and [[Matur Maker]]. His cousins also brought him under the guidance of Ed Smith, a coach who had helped direct them through their own basketball careers.{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Ben |title='A different path': Guardian of top recruit Makur Maker talks about Kentucky and the process |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article231641018.html |website=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |accessdate=30 July 2019 |date=18 June 2019}} Maker joined the basketball team with Matur and played in the National Preparatory Association and The Grind Session. In his next year, The Tech Academy closed, and he was [[homeschooling|homeschooled]]. Maker suffered a foot injury that sidelined him for the 2017–18 season.{{cite web |last1=Newman |first1=Logan |title=Why Makur Maker is transferring to Pacific Academy from Orange Lutheran |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/makur-maker-transfer-pacific-academy-orange-lutheran |website=USA Today high School Sports |accessdate=31 July 2019 |date=29 July 2019}} In the summer of 2018, he transferred to [[Lutheran High School of Orange County|Orange Lutheran High School]] in [[Orange, California]].{{cite web |last1=Gershon |first1=Josh |title=Makur Maker: Thon's cousin emerges as elite post in SoCal return |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Makur-Maker-Thons-cousin-emerges-as-elite-2020-post-prospect-in-SoCal-return-125903288/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=30 July 2019 |date=4 December 2018}} As a junior, he earned All-[[Trinity League]] first team and ''[[Orange County Register]]'' All-County second team honors.{{cite web |last1=Sondheimer |first1=Eric |title=Christian James of St. John Bosco is Trinity League MVP in basketball |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vti-trinity-basketball-20190311-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |accessdate=31 July 2019 |date=11 March 2019}}{{cite web |title=The Register's All-County boys basketball teams 2018–19 |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2019/03/26/the-registers-all-orange-county-boys-basketball-teams-for-2018-19-season/ |website=[[Orange County Register]] |accessdate=31 July 2019 |date=26 March 2019}} Maker faced eligibility questions entering his senior season, because he had already exhausted his eight semesters of eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Fryer |first1=Steve |title=Orange Lutheran's Makur Maker ineligible for 2019–20 boys basketball season |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2019/06/28/orange-lutherans-maker-confirmed-ineligible-for-coming-basketball-season/?platform=hootsuite |website=[[Orange County Register]] |accessdate=31 July 2019 |date=28 June 2019}} Instead of seeking a waiver from the [[California Interscholastic Federation]] to continue playing for Orange Lutheran, he transferred to Pacific Academy, a prep school in [[Irvine, California]], and continued his career with the affiliated program, Center of International Basketball Academy. On 17 October 2019, it was announced that he had submitted paperwork to explore his eligibility for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=No. 10 recruit Makur Maker petitions to be eligible for 2020 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27866921/no-10-recruit-makur-maker-petitions-eligible-2020-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=18 December 2019 |date=17 October 2019}} On 25 April 2020, he declared for the 2020 NBA draft. Despite finishing two credits short of high school graduation, Maker was granted eligibility by the NBA.{{cite web |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |title=Makur Maker entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29097584/sources-makur-maker-entering-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=25 April 2020 |date=25 April 2020}} However, on 3 August he withdrew from the draft to play college basketball.{{cite news |last1=Gaither |first1=Steven J. |title=Makur Maker opting out of NBA Draft |url=https://hbcugameday.com/2020/08/03/makur-maker-opting-out-of-nba-draft/ |accessdate=3 August 2020 |work=HBCU Gameday |date=3 August 2020}} ===Recruiting=== Maker was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[center (basketball)|centers]] in the 2020 recruiting class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web |last1=Byrum |first1=Tyler |title=Class of 2020 five-star prospect, Makur Maker is considering Howard in his final four |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/ncaa/class-2020-five-star-prospect-makur-maker-considering-howard-his-final-four |publisher=[[NBC Sports]] |accessdate=3 July 2020 |date=2 July 2020}} On 3 July 2020, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Howard Bison men's basketball|Howard]] over offers from [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]]. He became the highest-ranked recruit to commit to a [[Historically black colleges and universities|historically black college or university]] (HBCU) in the modern recruiting era. Maker made the decision in part to encourage future prospects to play for HBCU programs.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Five-star college basketball recruit Makur Maker commits to Howard over UCLA |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29403929/five-star-recruit-makur-maker-commits-howard-ucla |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=3 July 2020 |date=3 July 2020}} 2023, Maker played for the [[Liaoning Arctic Wolves]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]].
